predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Learners who spoke to a maintainer will record at least one behaviour of the existing system that contradicts its documentation.
predictions.instrument: the review movement's record. **If contradictions are rare, either the maintainers are not being asked the right question or the documentation in these estates is better than this design assumes, and the movement's justification should be revisited.**

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: A majority of first tool definitions will carry the upstream system's vocabulary in the tool name, despite the workflow instructing otherwise.
predictions.instrument: the submitted tool manifest, with each name coded *upstream* / *local* / *hybrid* by a second reader. **This predicts the failure of §4.1's own countermeasure**, and it is included because a countermeasure whose failure rate is unmeasured is an assumption.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: The `unfitting_case` field will take longer to write than every other field in the boundary decision combined, and a substantial share of submissions will leave it empty or generic.
predictions.instrument: self-reported time per field, plus the field coded *specific* / *generic* / *absent*. **This is the session's only direct test of its claim that the exceptions are where the maintenance goes**, and a null result would mean the claim is an aphorism rather than a design input.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: Learners instructed to compare their item-5 answer against the taught criterion (exercise 3) will produce non-integration entries judged specific more often than learners who read the same material without the comparison prompt.
predictions.instrument: a second reader's judgement, split within cohort on exercise-3 completion. **The same prediction is made across this module's sessions, so a null across all of them would indict the comparison pattern rather than any one session.**

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will answer opening item 3 with *nothing* or with something requiring permission.
predictions.instrument: the written answers, coded *nothing* / *requires permission* / *genuinely available* by a second reader, recorded before the review movement.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Available changes will more often be chosen for ease than for evidential value, judged by whether the learner can name who would read the result.
predictions.instrument: a single question put in the review movement, recorded per learner.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners unable to name a single foreclosing constraint will also be unable to name an addressee for the unfreezing argument.
predictions.instrument: the two fields, compared per learner. **If the two dissociate, the constraint-fog diagnosis is wrong and the single-constraint requirement should be reconsidered.**

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Unavailable designs written before the unfreezing argument will be more specific than those written after.
predictions.instrument: paired documents from a cohort where the order is deliberately reversed, judged unlabelled by a second reader. **This requires a cohort to be taught the session in the wrong order on purpose, which may not be defensible, and if it is not the prediction should be withdrawn rather than left unmeasurable.**

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: After provisioning the prototyping topology and reading its stated limitation, learners will more often name deployment topology as their foreclosing constraint than they did at [S026](/wiki/seminars/S026.md).
predictions.instrument: the foreclosing constraint named at S026 against the one named here, compared per learner. **If topology does not move up the list, the platform movement is a demonstration rather than an instrument**, and the session should say so rather than implying the provisioning changed anything.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: A minority of learners will present prototyping-topology evidence in their unfreezing argument without any statement of the topology it came from, despite the metric dimension carrying it.
predictions.instrument: the submitted argument, coded for whether the topology is stated in the prose and not only in the data. **This predicts the failure of §5's strongest countermeasure and is the direct test of §8's third objection**, and it is the prediction this paper would least like to lose.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: Fallback designs with a gating metric declared before the design was written will be judged *designed* rather than *diminished* by a second reader more often than those where it was declared after.
predictions.instrument: the two documents' timestamps against a blind judgement of the fallback. **This is the only test of §3.9's ordering claim**, and a null result would mean the gating metric is ceremony.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most first-pass comparisons will contain no experiment for at least one option.
predictions.instrument: the studies, counted by options with and without an experiment.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Refusals will be rarer than studies, including among learners whose opening item 1 answered that the choice was clear.
predictions.instrument: opening item 1 answers against the output produced, compared per learner. **If learners who said the choice was clear go on to produce studies, the negative rule is not transferring and the session's central instruction has failed.**

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: The agent's first use will produce at least one option not on the learner's shortlist more often when it is given criteria and constraints than when it is given the shortlist.
predictions.instrument: a cohort split on the prompt form, counting novel options returned.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: In the review movement, readers will reconstruct the criteria of studies containing experiments more often than the criteria of studies without them.
predictions.instrument: reconstruction success against experiment presence, per study.

predictions.label: Prediction 5.
predictions.claim: A majority of learners running the platform comparison will conclude that the correct answer is a different option per component rather than one option for the system, and a majority of those will nonetheless produce a study rather than a refusal.
predictions.instrument: the study's decision section coded *single option* / *per component*, against the output type produced. **If learners reach the per-component conclusion and still write studies, the negative rule has been understood and not adopted**, which is a different failure from not understanding it and needs a different countermeasure.

predictions.label: Prediction 6.
predictions.claim: Studies whose power note was written before any experiment ran will more often distinguish *no difference found* from *no difference detectable* in their results section.
predictions.instrument: the results section coded for that distinction, split on whether the power note preceded the experiments. **This is the only test of §4.2's addition to the specification**, and a null result would mean the field is ceremony and should be removed rather than defended.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: A minority of studies will carry an externally published magnitude — a speedup, a recall figure, a cost multiple — without its baseline or workload profile, despite the material treating exactly that as the failure.
predictions.instrument: the studies, scanned for imported figures and coded for whether the baseline is stated. **This predicts the failure of §5's weakest countermeasure**, and it is included because a countermeasure whose failure rate is unmeasured is an assumption.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.

predictions.instrument: the reader's response, coded *missed headings* / *missed none*, against the scope chosen.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Item 5 will be the most frequently failed specification item, and item 6 the least.
predictions.instrument: per-item pass rates, reported without aggregation.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: The register walk will surface at least one constraint per candidate that the design neither accommodates nor violates — a constraint that was never real.
predictions.instrument: the walk's record, counting entries with nowhere to point, classified by the candidate as *violated* or *not real*.

predictions.claim: Candidates whose scope defence was drafted before the design will change scope more often than those who drafted them together.
predictions.instrument: the submission ordering against any recorded scope change. **If no candidate ever changes scope, the defence is decorative and the movement should be rewritten as a declaration.**

predictions.label: Prediction 5.

predictions.label: Prediction 7.
predictions.claim: Candidates who withheld their decision from the instrument will paste arguments judged more specific than those who supplied it.
predictions.instrument: a within-cohort split on the prompt form recorded at exercise 2, with the pasted arguments coded *specific* / *generic* by a second reader. **If the two prompt forms produce indistinguishable output, the instruction to withhold is ceremony and should be removed rather than repeated.**

predictions.label: Prediction 8.
predictions.claim: Candidates instructed to compare their item-3 answer against the taught criterion (exercise 3) will more often change scope than candidates who read the same material without the comparison prompt.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will produce a first-draft trigger whose first step is performed by their own team.
predictions.instrument: the specification's first step, coded by actor as *delivery team* / *register* / *other party*.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: The untagged environment will be missed more often than the personally issued credential.
predictions.instrument: presence or absence of each of the three traps in the submitted specification, tallied per learner.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Evidence artefacts will more often be located inside the delivery team's own tooling than in a place a customer-side party could reach.
predictions.instrument: the evidence column, coded by location as *delivery-side* / *customer-side* / *shared* / *unstated*.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: After the register role-play, learners will add steps rather than remove them, and the added steps will name external parties.
predictions.instrument: the diff between pre-role-play and post-role-play specifications, with added steps coded by actor. **If learners instead add steps performed by themselves, the role-play has taught thoroughness rather than mechanisation** and should be redesigned. **None of these has been measured.**

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most first submissions will fail item 9.
predictions.instrument: the taper field, coded *date stated* / *no date* / *no taper*, on first submission.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners who accept the challenger's easy offer will produce fully owned manifests, and will describe the occasion afterwards as having gone well.
predictions.instrument: the owner column against the post-occasion self-report, paired per learner.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Withdrawal specifications will be longer than manifests for a substantial share of the cohort.
predictions.instrument: a length comparison of the two artefacts, reported as a distribution and never as a threshold.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Item 10 will discriminate more strongly between learners than any of the nine written items.
predictions.instrument: the pass rate per item across the cohort. **If item 10 does not discriminate, the live defence is redundant at this occasion** and the assessment should become a written submission, which would be cheaper and should then be done. **None of these has been measured.**

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will propose an instruction-shaped intervention for at least three of the four states at opening item 4.
predictions.instrument: the written answers, coded per state as *instruction* / *authority* / *engagement* / *practice* / *other* by a second reader.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Most first-draft capability statements will express at least one act as a topic.
predictions.instrument: the review movement's single question, recorded as answerable or not per act.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: The credential-holding third party will be omitted from first drafts more often than either named group.
predictions.instrument: presence of each of the three groups in the pre-review draft.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Learners will record the willing group's current state more optimistically than the unwilling group's, at equal observed evidence.
predictions.instrument: current-state ratings against the evidence cited for each, read by an assessor blind to which group is which. **If this fails, the session's warning about mistaking willingness for ability is unnecessary at this stage** and should move to [S079](/wiki/seminars/S079.md), where it costs less. **None of these has been measured.**

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Nearly every learner will answer opening item 5 immediately, and few will have the answer recorded anywhere in their existing plan.
predictions.instrument: the written answers against the plan's contents, coded *recorded* / *not recorded*.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: First-draft plans will place most dated transfer items in the second half of the remaining schedule.
predictions.instrument: item dates against the schedule midpoint, reported as a distribution.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: The item another learner predicts will break first will match the item the learner later reclaims, where a reclaim occurs.
predictions.instrument: the review movement's prediction against the reclaim record. **If these do not match, the review movement is entertainment** and should be replaced by a written pre-commitment.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Learners will respond to the technology function's refusal by redrafting the plan rather than by recording unwillingness.
predictions.instrument: the post-refusal artefact, coded *plan revised* / *unwillingness recorded* / *escalated* / *abandoned*. **None of these has been measured.**

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: First-draft inventories will contain more technical than organisational dependencies.
predictions.instrument: inventory lines coded *technical* / *organisational* / *comprehension* by a second reader.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Absent the forcing requirement, most disposal records would be entirely documentary.
predictions.instrument: the disposal column on the pre-requirement draft where one is collected, tallied by decision type.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: The dependency named at opening item 3 will more often be disposed as *transfer* or *document* than as *simplify away* or *remove*.
predictions.instrument: the item-3 answer matched to its disposal decision. **If this fails, the pleasing-dependency diagnostic is not detecting what the session claims** and item 3 should be replaced.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Few learners will write a commercial position when their situation implies one.
predictions.instrument: presence or absence of the commercial paragraph, against whether the supplied situation makes continued involvement plausible. **None of these has been measured.**

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will intervene at least once, and most interventions will fall outside the written condition.
predictions.instrument: the intervention count and the condition text, coded *inside* / *outside* by a second reader.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners who select the enthusiastic operator will record fewer incapacities than those who select the responsibility-holder.
predictions.instrument: operator identity against the incapacity count.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Rehearsals with no recorded incapacity will more often lack a named avoided difficulty than rehearsals with one.
predictions.instrument: the two record fields, cross-tabulated.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: A substantial share of observed incapacities will produce a note rather than a change to an owner, a dependency, a date or the decision.
predictions.instrument: the obligation field, coded *changed something* / *note only*. **If most produce notes, the obligation clause is inert** and the session should require the change to be made in the record before the session closes rather than asserted. **None of these has been measured.**

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: A substantial share of learners will accept the challenger's easy exit, and most of those will describe the occasion afterwards as having gone well.
predictions.instrument: the acceptance record's signatory against the post-occasion self-report.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often present evidence against their own decision when their rehearsal produced a recorded incapacity than when it did not.
predictions.instrument: the defence transcript, coded for self-presented counter-evidence, against the rehearsal record's incapacity field.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Decisions of *do not leave yet* will more often lack a named observer and date than decisions to leave will lack a stated ground.
predictions.instrument: both decision types coded for completeness against their respective standards.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Independent assessor levels will diverge by more than one sub-level on a noticeable share of learners, and divergence will concentrate on learners who refused to leave.
predictions.instrument: the paired independent judgements before deliberation, with divergence cross-tabulated against decision type. **If divergence concentrates on refusals, the occasion is under-specified for that decision** and the standard for a refusal needs writing, not the scale. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this occasion, and the programme's own position is that most predictions in this wiki will never be measured at all.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will produce at least one procedure step that a stranger cannot execute, and most of those steps will be an imperative with no object.
predictions.instrument: the procedures, coded step by step for executability by a reader without the brief, with the imperative-with-no-object form counted separately.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often mark a dimension unreachable when their adversarial re-derivation disagreed with them than when it agreed.
predictions.instrument: the unreachable list against the recorded agent transcript.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners who report a lower re-derived position will place that report later in their artefact than learners reporting a higher one place theirs.
predictions.instrument: position of the finding within the document, against its direction.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: A noticeable share of learners will produce a critique of maturity instruments in place of a procedure.
predictions.instrument: the artefacts, classified as procedure, critique, or both. **If this share is large, §1 of this paper is doing the damage** and the session's opening should be moved after the working movement rather than before it. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will produce at least one position whose supporting evidence is a capability rather than an act, on the first attempt.
predictions.instrument: the positions, coded per row for evidence type by a second reader.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often name a role whose work got worse when their diagnosis concerned the reverted site than when it concerned a group that never started.
predictions.instrument: the item-4 answers cross-tabulated against the group diagnosed.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Where the diagnosis is a willingness problem, the proposed intervention will more often be instructional than where the diagnosis is a knowledge problem.
predictions.instrument: diagnosis and intervention coded independently and paired. **If this does not hold, the training reflex this session is built on is not present in this population** and §1 should be rewritten as a caution rather than as a premise.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Learners who list unobservable groups explicitly will more often name the managed-service supplier than those who do not list any.
predictions.instrument: the unobserved list, checked for the supplier. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: In most submissions the unpaid version will be shorter and less specific than the paid one, measured by the presence of named owners, triggers and artefacts rather than by length alone.
predictions.instrument: both parts coded for the four specificity elements, compared within submission.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners who write the unpaid version first, as instructed, will more often name an owner employed by the customer than those who report writing both together.
predictions.instrument: the named owner against the self-reported working order.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Most conflict-of-interest statements will describe the organisation's interest and omit the author's own.
predictions.instrument: the statements, coded for whose interest is named.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: The closing question will produce more *I do not know* answers than either alternative.
predictions.instrument: the answers, recorded verbatim and classified. **If it produces almost none, the question is being heard as a test with a correct answer** and it should be replaced rather than repeated. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most learners will classify the perpetually regenerating item correctly and will still produce a note rather than a decision for it.
predictions.instrument: the findings, coded for classification and separately for whether an owner and a trigger were named.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Criterion changes will more often be proposed than costed.
predictions.instrument: the proposals, checked for whose time, against what other work, and with what maintenance expectation.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners whose closing sentence names a proposition will more often have classified all regenerated items than those whose closing sentence names a count.
predictions.instrument: the closing sentences, classified as proposition or count, cross-tabulated with classification completeness.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Where the honest answer is that only the list improved, most learners will not say so.
predictions.instrument: the closing sentences, against an independent reading of whether anything about the system changed. **If most do say so, this session's premise about the discomfort of an unfinished list is wrong for this population** and §1 should be rewritten. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most executors will encounter at least one step they cannot perform, and most authors will not have predicted it.
predictions.instrument: the execution records against the sealed predictions, matched per step.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will classify divergences as absent evidence more readily than as a bad rule, even where the evidence exists and the rule is at fault.
predictions.instrument: the reconciliations coded per divergence, checked against the executor's record of what they inspected.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Divergences in the flattering direction — where the executor reached a higher position — will receive shorter treatment in the reconciliation than divergences in the other direction.
predictions.instrument: the reconciliation, with treatment length and specificity coded by direction.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Independent assessor levels will diverge by more than one sub-level on a noticeable share of learners, and divergence will concentrate on learners whose procedure defeated their executor early.
predictions.instrument: paired independent judgements before deliberation, cross-tabulated with the execution's stopping point. **If divergence concentrates there, the occasion cannot distinguish a bad procedure from an incomplete observation** and the standard for an early stop needs writing. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this occasion, and the programme's own position is that most predictions in this wiki will never be measured at all.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most provenance entries on a first attempt will name a person or a team rather than an observation or a record.
predictions.instrument: the ledgers, coded per row against the survives-the-person test.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often produce an observable staleness signal for items bound to a platform than for items bound to a customer's process.
predictions.instrument: the signal field, coded observable or scheduled, cross-tabulated with item type.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: The retirement chosen will more often be an item of low value than the item the learner most resents retiring, despite the instruction.
predictions.instrument: the retirement, against the learner's own stated resentment ranking collected separately.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Few learners will reach for the environment-reuse parallel without prompting.
predictions.instrument: the artefacts and the session record, checked for the reference before the facilitator supplies it. **If most do reach for it, the retrieval from [S074](/wiki/seminars/S074.md) is stronger than the design assumed** and the session can afford to spend its time elsewhere. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most loop specifications will name a queue, a team or a system at receipt rather than a person or a role.
predictions.instrument: the specifications, coded at the receipt step.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: The reporter-return step will be the most frequently omitted of the six, despite being last in a fixed order.
predictions.instrument: the six steps, checked for completion, counted by step.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often invent a process for their own organisation than record a blank, on the first attempt.
predictions.instrument: the specifications against a follow-up question asking where each answer came from.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Most learners will identify the writing as the loop's weakest link.
predictions.instrument: the closing statements, classified by which of receipt, obligation, ownership, states, closure, return or writing was named. **If most name receipt or return, the session's premise is already held by this population** and the working movement can be shortened. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: On a first attempt the verified class will be the longest of the four in most registers.
predictions.instrument: the registers, with entries counted by class.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Magnitudes will appear in the cited class in a noticeable share of registers, most often as a range rather than as a point.
predictions.instrument: the cited-class entries, coded for any quantity.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Undermining results will more often concern the measurement than the system.
predictions.instrument: the mandatory entry, classified by subject. **If the undermining result is nearly always about the baseline, the requirement is being satisfied by the easiest available admission** and the standard needs a second clause.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Exclusions will more often name topics than interests.
predictions.instrument: the exclusion list, coded topic or interest, against the three prompting questions. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most first-attempt amendments will be advisory in effect while being presented as binding.
predictions.instrument: the amendments, coded for whether the named mechanism can fail without a person's cooperation.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Learners will more often produce an occasion for an amendment concerning an artefact they authored than for one concerning a process they were subject to.
predictions.instrument: the occasions, classified by whether the learner was author or subject.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Declined amendments will be shorter than proposed ones despite the equal-length requirement.
predictions.instrument: both, compared within submission for specificity rather than for word count.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Few learners will report a contradiction in the practice rather than resolving one silently.
predictions.instrument: the submissions, checked for a reported contradiction against the set of contradictions known to be present in the supplied practice. **If none is reported, the supplied practice does not contain a findable one** and the situation needs rebuilding rather than the session. **None of these has been measured.** No cohort has run this session.

predictions.label: Prediction 1.
predictions.claim: Most forward briefs will contain more lines claiming limitation than lines claiming unsupervised competence, and the unsupervised claims will be pitched at narrower activities.
predictions.instrument: the briefs, with lines counted by type and coded for activity granularity.

predictions.label: Prediction 2.
predictions.claim: Divergence between the learner's reading and the assessors' levels will fall predominantly in the direction of learner understatement.
predictions.instrument: paired readings, with direction of divergence recorded per learner. **If divergence is predominantly overstatement, §1's account of the two pressures is wrong for this population** and the occasion's framing must be rewritten rather than its instrument.

predictions.label: Prediction 3.
predictions.claim: Learners who engaged with divergence rather than deferring to it will more often have named an occasion in every line of their brief.
predictions.instrument: the live record coded for deferral, against the briefs coded for occasion completeness.

predictions.label: Prediction 4.
predictions.claim: Answers to the fixed closing question will more often name what the learner will get wrong than who will notice.
predictions.instrument: the answers, coded for both halves. **None of these has been measured, and the wider statement belongs here rather than in a footnote.** Every paper in this wiki closes with predictions naming an instrument, and not one of those instruments has been applied to anybody. No cohort has run this programme. **The design's own position, stated where it is least convenient, is that most of these predictions will never be measured at all** — and a body of work that predicts its own instrumentation will not be executed has conceded something about itself that its sources never conceded about theirs.

teaching_moves.text: The organisation that named this role says in public that it cannot specify the skills the role requires. What does that mean for a programme claiming to teach them? **Item 3 is the one that matters, and most answers to it are wrong in the same direction.** People assume the decision is theirs because they wrote the code.

teaching_moves.label: Defence by repetition
teaching_moves.text: under pressure you say the same thing with more emphasis. *Warning sign:* your third answer contains no information your first did not.

teaching_moves.label: The control mistaken for a check
teaching_moves.text: the safeguard you demand is an instruction somebody may follow. *Warning sign:* your evaluation cannot fail unless a person forgets to do something.

teaching_moves.label: The unchosen unit
teaching_moves.text: a score is reported without its split strategy. *Warning sign:* you cannot say whether your number is about the last answer or the whole trajectory, and you did not notice the difference.

teaching_moves.label: The inherited threshold
teaching_moves.text: a cut point arrives from a default and is defended as a standard. *Warning sign:* asked why that threshold, your answer describes the tool rather than the harm.

teaching_moves.text: The workshop ends. Everyone thanks you warmly and says it was the best session they have had this year. Nothing else happens. **Did it work?**
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.text: Name the single decision this workshop exists to make. Who in the room has the authority to make it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.text: What observable thing, present at the end of the second day, would tell you the workshop had failed?
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.text: Somebody proposes holding it at your offices because the rooms are better. What information do you need before you can agree?
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.text: If the answer to item 1 is *no*, what were the other people in the room being asked to give up? **Item 5 is the one this session is really about.** Items 1 to 4 can be answered from good instincts. Item 5 requires you to have a theory of what a workshop extracts from the people attending it, and most learners discover while writing it that they do not have one — which is why the warm thanks felt like enough. **Most people answer item 1 with a qualified yes.** They will say it built relationships, or created alignment, or opened the door. Hold that answer; the session is going to argue against it, and the argument is not obvious.
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.label: The demonstration.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* the customer asks for a tool overview, and you agree because it seems like a reasonable warm-up. The session degrades into a walkthrough of what your tooling can do; the customer enjoys it and learns nothing about themselves.
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.label: The alignment claim.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* your charter's success condition uses a word that has no failure state. The stated output is agreement, shared understanding or a common language — none observable at the end, all assertable afterwards.
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.label: The room of watchers.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* the invitation list grew and nobody was removed from it. Attendance is decided by seniority and interest rather than by authority and hands.
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.label: The prepared agenda.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* you could run the same two days for a different customer without changing a slide. The structure was settled before anybody understood the situation, so the session can only produce answers the structure already allows.
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.label: The convenient venue.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* the venue was decided before the difficulty was named. Cost and comfort chose the location, and the people who could have answered the hard question could not travel.
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.label: The endorsement question.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* a question in your protocol contains the name of a product category you sell. You have asked the customer to validate your solution and will record their politeness as evidence.
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.label: The polished protocol.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* your topic is elaborate and you have not run it against a hostile respondent. Detail added early drags the discussion onto irrelevancies, and polish suppresses honest feedback.
teaching_moves.day_title: S011 · What a Workshop Is For, and What It Is Not
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio topic and trigger design — an elicitation protocol made explicit, where the ordering of questions is a designed artefact rather than a habit

teaching_moves.text: List every condition that would have to be true for this session to be worth running. Now mark each one **customer**, **us** or **platform**.
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.text: Look at your marks. How many are **us**?
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.text: The session runs badly. Write the sentence your organisation will use to explain why. Whose fault does it assign?
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.text: Your sponsor says a condition cannot be met but asks you to proceed anyway. Under what circumstances is that the right answer, and what gets recorded?
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.text: What is the difference between a condition and a preference? **Item 2 is the session.** Most readiness lists point outward. A list that points only outward cannot fail in a way that implicates the person holding it — and a list with no platform row cannot fail at all until the room is watching.
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.label: The disposition gate.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* your gate would let you explain any bad outcome without changing anything you do. Every condition describes the customer's attitude — engaged, open to change, willing to invest. Attitudes are unfalsifiable in advance and infinitely available as explanations afterwards.
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.label: The waived prerequisite.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* the document that lists the conditions also contains the words *even if*. Conditions are stated and then followed by an offer to proceed regardless. **They are therefore not conditions.**
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.label: The unrecorded waiver.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* you can say a waiver happened but not who owns it. Everybody remembers agreeing; nobody wrote down who decided.
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.label: Readiness theatre.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* the gate has never once come back unmet. It is completed because completion is required, by the person whose session it would block.
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.label: The gate that only points outward.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* nothing in your gate could be fixed by doing more work yourself.
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.label: The undated premise.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* you can state the platform constraint and cannot say when you last checked it or where. A premise carried from the last engagement is a memory, and memories do not expire visibly.
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.label: Absence read as denial.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* your finding column says the documentation does not support something, when what you observed is that the documentation does not mention it. **A silence bounds your knowledge, not the product.**
teaching_moves.day_title: S012 · Readiness, and the Workshop You Should Not Run
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Learn MCP Server — pre-checking the platform premises a workshop would otherwise spend its time discovering

teaching_moves.text: A participant states something about their own pipeline that you know to be wrong. What do you do, and when?
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.text: You ask a question. Nobody answers for eight seconds. What do you do?
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.text: Half the room is remote. Name the specific thing that will go wrong, and the specific person whose job it is to prevent it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.text: Somebody has not spoken all morning. List three different reasons that might be true, only one of which is about them.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.text: You have run the session, well, four days in a row. What is the fifth day worse at? **Item 2 is where most engineers fail.** The instinct is to rescue the silence by offering options, and the options are the answer. Item 4 is the one the session will spend most of its time on, because two of your three reasons will be about the person and the third will be the one that matters.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.label: The expert in the chair.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* you have used the words "actually" or "just to be precise". You correct a factual error during the session and authority transfers to you; everything after that is a conversation with you rather than about them.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.label: The rescued silence.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* your question ended with "for example" or with a list. You fill a pause with example answers and the response set narrows to the examples.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.label: The two-tier room.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* nobody remote has spoken unprompted since the first ten minutes. The people in the room have a session and the people on the call have a broadcast.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.label: Encouragement instead of structure.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* the invitation to speak and the shape of the question disagree. You tell people there are no wrong answers, then ask one that has an obviously right one.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.label: Wellness as advice.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* the guidance about your capacity lives somewhere that does not schedule your time. You know you should not run five of these in a row, and the schedule was made by somebody reading a different document.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.label: The mechanical wait.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* you waited through a silence in which somebody was visibly struggling, because waiting is the technique. Silence is read differently by different people, and a rule applied without reading the room is a habit rather than a skill.
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.label: Shape mistaken for quality.
teaching_moves.text: *Warning sign:* your constraints all held and you cannot say what you learned. An enforceable prohibition tells you the question had the right form. **It cannot tell you the question was worth asking.**
teaching_moves.day_title: S013 · Facilitation as a Technical Skill
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: GitHub Copilot custom chat modes and instructions files — constraining what an agent may ask and in what order, as facilitation encoded and inspectable

teaching_moves.text: Somebody says: *we tried this three years ago and it did not work.* What are your next two sentences?
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.text: A participant has not spoken for an hour. Write down what you will do. Now write what would happen if the reason is that their manager is in the room.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.text: You cannot answer a question. What are your options, and which of them costs you least later?
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.text: You are running behind. Name the thing you will cut, and say who decides.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.text: Which of the situations above would you rather handle badly than handle by breaking a rule? **Item 5 has an answer and most people do not have it yet.** By the end of the session you should. Item 3 is the one that will surprise you, because the option that costs least later is the one that feels worst at the time, and you will be able to name it only after you have watched somebody else take it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.label: Marking yourself on recovery
teaching_moves.text: you judge the handling by whether the room came back, so any intervention that worked is retrospectively correct. *Warning sign:* your account of the moment contains the word "eventually" and no account of what you were tempted to do.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.label: Converting the sceptic
teaching_moves.text: you answer their objection, well, with evidence. They stop objecting. They also stop telling you what will actually block this. *Warning sign:* the room got easier and you learned nothing new.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.label: Reading silence as agreement
teaching_moves.text: nobody objected, so the proposal is accepted. *Warning sign:* your notes record consensus and cannot name who expressed it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.label: Answering the unanswerable
teaching_moves.text: you produce a plausible answer to a question outside your knowledge, because not knowing feels like a failure of the competence you were selected for. *Warning sign:* you are speaking in the conditional and nobody has written anything down.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.label: The silent cut
teaching_moves.text: you are behind, so you shorten the exercise where the customer works and keep the part where you present. *Warning sign:* the schedule slipped and your own speaking time did not.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.label: The dominating participant as the customer
teaching_moves.text: one voice answers everything, and your notes become that person's view of their organisation. *Warning sign:* your consolidated finding at [S018](/wiki/seminars/S018.md) traces to one informant.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.label: Disagreement routed as malfunction
teaching_moves.text: your escalation treats a sceptic the same way it treats a misunderstanding, and tries again. *Warning sign:* your design has two failure classes and the room has three.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.label: The handover with no recipient
teaching_moves.text: the conversation stops and passes to "a human", or the record says the situation was escalated and cannot say to whom. *Warning sign:* the same sentence would be true if nobody received it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S014 · The Difficult Room
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Copilot Studio escalation and fallback design — what a conversation does when it stops going well, and who it hands to

teaching_moves.text: Which of your four artefacts — charter, gate, facilitation plan, rehearsal record — do you expect to abandon first when the session goes wrong?
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.text: Your gate has an unmet condition on the morning. Do you run? Who decides, and what gets written?
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.text: At the end, a participant says they are excited and will "definitely look at getting some time booked". Is that a commitment?
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.text: What will you record if nobody commits to anything?
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.text: What would make this session's finding wrong? **Item 5 is the one the assessment is really about.** Items 1 to 4 you can answer from the module. Item 5 requires you to state a finding in a form that has a falsifier attached, and most candidates discover while writing it that what they were going to record has no falsifier because it is not a claim about the customer's world.
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.label: The abandoned charter
teaching_moves.text: the session drifts, the charter stays in the folder, and the closing record describes what happened rather than what was decided. *Warning sign:* you have not looked at the charter since the first hour.
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.label: The retrospective waiver
teaching_moves.text: a condition was unmet, the session ran, and the waiver is written afterwards in the passive voice. *Warning sign:* the record says the condition was waived and cannot say by whom.
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.label: Interest banked as commitment
teaching_moves.text: a warm sentence about future intent is written into the closing record as a next step. *Warning sign:* the recorded commitment has no person, no date and no cost to anybody.
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.label: The rescued difficulty
teaching_moves.text: you handled the assigned difficulty by breaking a prohibition, it worked, and you are pleased. *Warning sign:* your account of the moment is about the outcome.
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.label: The smoothed absence
teaching_moves.text: nobody committed, and the record says the session built strong foundations. *Warning sign:* the closing record's most concrete noun is "alignment".
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.label: The unfalsifiable finding
teaching_moves.text: the specification's falsifiers are conditions nobody could observe, or are restatements of the finding with a negative in front. *Warning sign:* you cannot name who would see the falsifier fire.
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.label: The debriefed record
teaching_moves.text: the closing record was written after the room agreed what had happened. *Warning sign:* your record uses a phrase somebody else used first.
teaching_moves.day_title: S015 · Running a Workshop End to End ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Foundry prompt agents — capturing a workshop's output as a declarative agent specification, then using the agent to attack the specification

teaching_moves.text: A question in the bank asks where the customer thinks an assistant could help their engineers. **Who benefits from the answer?**

teaching_moves.text: Every question ships with example answers. Name one thing that changes about the response when the examples are read out.

teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Agent Framework evaluations — building an evaluator for leading questions, and discovering it agrees with you more readily than it should

teaching_moves.text: What question would tell you this engagement should not proceed?
teaching_moves.day_title: S016 · Questions That Invite Flattering Answers
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Microsoft Agent Framework evaluations — building an evaluator for leading questions, and discovering it agrees with you more readily than it should

teaching_moves.text: options down the side, criteria across the top, and weighted scores that are opinions with arithmetic performed on them. No experiment anywhere. *Warning sign:* your study could have been written without touching anything.

teaching_moves.label: The specification its own author does not meet
teaching_moves.text: **the only worked comparison published alongside this template omits several of the sections the template requires and renames another.** A learner copying the example would fail the specification. Pages read 2026-07-30. *Warning sign:* you are following an example rather than the specification, and have not compared the two.

teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Foundry hosted agents, Copilot Studio and the serverless agents runtime compared across authoring model, hosting and cost for one stated requirement

teaching_moves.label: The single-option study
teaching_moves.text: one real candidate and one straw candidate, present to satisfy the floor. *Warning sign:* the second option has no experiment because nobody was ever going to run one.
teaching_moves.day_title: S029 · Trade Studies, and When Not to Run One
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Foundry hosted agents, Copilot Studio and the serverless agents runtime compared across authoring model, hosting and cost for one stated requirement

teaching_moves.label: The criterion added after the result
teaching_moves.text: the evidence came back inconveniently and a new consideration appeared. *Warning sign:* the criterion that decided it is not in the decision record that opened the study.
teaching_moves.day_title: S029 · Trade Studies, and When Not to Run One
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Foundry hosted agents, Copilot Studio and the serverless agents runtime compared across authoring model, hosting and cost for one stated requirement

teaching_moves.label: The unbounded study
teaching_moves.text: the comparison expands to include everything, and the decision it existed to inform is taken elsewhere while it runs. *Warning sign:* nobody is waiting for it any more.
teaching_moves.day_title: S029 · Trade Studies, and When Not to Run One
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: Foundry hosted agents, Copilot Studio and the serverless agents runtime compared across authoring model, hosting and cost for one stated requirement

teaching_moves.label: The underpowered experiment
teaching_moves.text: each option was tried, briefly, and the differences were within the noise. *Warning sign:* you cannot say what difference your experiment could have detected.
