teaching_moves.text: What decision does this design commit you to, and for how long?
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.text: At what scope should it be written — a task, a feature, a milestone, or an investigation?
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.text: **Name the heading your chosen scope requires that the scope below it does not.**
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.text: Who runs this after it exists?
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.text: What in your design is still open, and are you allowed to leave it open? **Items 3 and 4 are the same question.** The published convention this session uses escalates from feature scope to milestone scope by adding exactly one heading, and that heading is about operation. A design that leaves the scope of a single piece of work **acquires a runtime owner**, and that acquisition is the whole content of the escalation.
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.label: The essay at every scope
teaching_moves.text: one document shape for all decisions, so a task-sized choice arrives with a milestone's ceremony and a milestone-sized choice arrives with a task's. *Warning sign:* your defence of the scope choice is about the size of the document.
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.label: The milestone design with no operational owner
teaching_moves.text: the design commits somebody to running the thing and nobody is named. This is the failure the escalation exists to catch and it is the commonest one. *Warning sign:* item 4 was answered with a team that has not agreed.
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.label: The open question that is a decision nobody wants to take
teaching_moves.text: it is listed as open because listing it is easier than resolving it, and it names nobody who could close it. *Warning sign:* the same question was open at [S024](/wiki/seminars/S024.md).
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.label: The fully mitigated risk register
teaching_moves.text: every risk has a mitigation, several of the mitigations are the word *monitor*, and nothing is carried. *Warning sign:* nothing in your design worries you.
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.label: The perpetual draft
teaching_moves.text: the in-progress marking has been on the document for weeks and has stopped meaning anything. *Warning sign:* somebody asks whether it is finished.
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.label: The design with unauthored constraints
teaching_moves.text: the frozen inputs are attached and none of them has an authority, so the design is built on the register's weakest entries. *Warning sign:* the attached register is the first version, unchanged since [S026](/wiki/seminars/S026.md).
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.label: The context that leaks the decision
teaching_moves.text: the record's context section is written after the choice and a reader can state the conclusion from it alone. *Warning sign:* your context contains a comparative adjective.
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.label: The straw rejection
teaching_moves.text: the rejected option is recorded in the weakest form anybody has ever put it in, so the record cannot be reopened honestly when the constraint moves. *Warning sign:* the adversarial reading is shorter than your own reasoning for the option you chose.
teaching_moves.day_title: S030 · A Design at the Scope of Its Decision ⊘
teaching_moves.platform_anchor: An architecture decision record in which the agent is made to argue the rejected option at its strongest

teaching_moves.text: Name the one thing in your design that might not work. Now write the question whose answer would tell you.
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.text: What would you do differently on Monday if the answer were no?
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.text: You spend a week finding out and the answer is yes. What happens to the code you wrote?
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.text: Somebody asks what you recommend. You have run the investigation. Why might the honest answer be that recommending is not your job here?
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.text: A colleague generated a working version of the risky part in an afternoon. Is that a spike? **Item 3 is the one the session cares about.** Almost everybody says the code is kept. It is the answer the tooling makes obvious, it is the answer that costs nothing to give, and it is the answer that converts an investigation into an unreviewed foundation.
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.label: The spike that becomes the product
teaching_moves.text: the code works, the deadline arrives, and the investigation ships. *Warning sign:* your charter has no disposal line, or the disposal line has no date.
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.label: The recommendation in the goal
teaching_moves.text: the charter's question is *which should we choose*, so the investigation is a decision wearing an investigation's costume. *Warning sign:* your question contains the word *best*.
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.label: The unbounded enquiry
teaching_moves.text: the spike ends when the person doing it feels finished. *Warning sign:* your bound is expressed as a feeling about sufficiency.
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.label: The uncontested question
teaching_moves.text: the answer changes nothing, because the decision was already taken. *Warning sign:* nobody can tell you what happens on Monday if the answer is no.
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.label: The generated foundation
teaching_moves.text: an agent produced something that runs, and its running is treated as the finding. *Warning sign:* your evidence is that the code executed.
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.label: The day-one prototype
teaching_moves.text: a reusable starting point produced something impressive before anybody established what should be built. *Warning sign:* you have an artefact and no charter.
teaching_moves.day_title: S031 · The Spike, and Why Its Code Is Discarded

teaching_moves.text: Your engagement has failed. It is over, it is public, and the reason is known. Write the reason.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.text: Write four more, and make at least two of them non-technical.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.text: Which of your five would somebody in the room have been reluctant to say out loud on day one? Why?
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.text: For each of the five, name the cheapest thing that would tell you now whether it is happening.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.text: Which of them are you going to accept rather than act on, and who owns that acceptance? **Item 1 is stated as a fact in the past tense, and the grammar is the instrument.** *What could go wrong* invites a list of hedged possibilities. *It failed — why* invites an account. Notice which one you found easier.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.label: The risk register in fancy dress
teaching_moves.text: the causes are hedged, conditional and generic, and could have been written about any project. *Warning sign:* your causes contain the words *may*, *could* or *potentially*.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.label: The polite pre-mortem
teaching_moves.text: the real cause is known to three people in the room and none of them says it. *Warning sign:* nothing on the list would embarrass anybody present.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.label: The all-technical failure
teaching_moves.text: every cause is an engineering cause, in a discipline whose own material says resistance originates in ownership of process rather than in technical incapacity. *Warning sign:* no row names a person's interests.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.label: The ratified plan
teaching_moves.text: the pre-mortem is run after the plan is fixed, so nothing it produces can change anything. *Warning sign:* the record's outputs are all *monitor*.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.label: The unowned acceptance
teaching_moves.text: a cause is accepted by the group, which means by nobody. *Warning sign:* an owner column with blanks in it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.label: The exhaustive list
teaching_moves.text: forty causes, none routed, filed. *Warning sign:* the record took longer to produce than the cheapest test on it would have taken to run.
teaching_moves.day_title: S032 · The Pre-Mortem

teaching_moves.text: Take your design's riskiest claim and write it as a question a test could answer. Now write the answer format: a number, a yes, a transcript, a count, a demonstration.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.text: Which of your uncertainties can be settled by talking to somebody, and which cannot? Sort them.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.text: Somebody demonstrates the hard part working, once, on an example they chose. What have you learned?
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.text: A model produces a fluent, confident, well-structured answer to something you cannot check. What is your position?
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.text: What is the cheapest thing that could stop this engagement, and have you done it yet? **Item 3 is the trap.** A successful demonstration on a chosen example establishes that the thing is possible on that example, which is a much smaller claim than the one it will be reported as.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.label: The unanswerable question
teaching_moves.text: *can we do this* has no answer format, so the answer will be somebody's confidence. *Warning sign:* your question could be answered by nodding.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.label: The demonstration mistaken for feasibility
teaching_moves.text: it worked once, on an example the demonstrator chose. *Warning sign:* nobody selected the input.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.label: The merged classes
teaching_moves.text: a market question and a technical question share a row and a test. *Warning sign:* your instrument for *will the model do this* is a stakeholder interview.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.label: The persuasive wrong answer
teaching_moves.text: the output was fluent, structured and confident, and it was accepted. *Warning sign:* your check on the answer is that it looked right.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.label: The interesting first
teaching_moves.text: you spiked the part you wanted to build. *Warning sign:* your cheapest disqualifier is still unrun in week three.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.label: The deferred question
teaching_moves.text: feasibility is scheduled into the build, where it becomes a defect rather than a decision. *Warning sign:* a row whose instrument is *we will find out in delivery*.
teaching_moves.day_title: S033 · Feasibility as a Question with an Answer

teaching_moves.text: Name every data dependency in your design. For each, write who told you it existed.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.text: For each, write what you have personally looked at. Be precise: a schema, a sample, a document describing it, or nothing.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.text: Somebody offers to send you an extract next week. What have you learned in the meantime?
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.text: The field you need is present in every row. Under what circumstances is that bad news?
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.text: The data was collected for one purpose and you intend to use it for another. Whose question is that, and have you asked them? **Item 2 is the finding.** Most learners discover that their entire data position rests on descriptions, and that nobody on the team has seen a row.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.label: The promised extract
teaching_moves.text: the whole position rests on something arriving later, and the schedule assumes it arrives correct. *Warning sign:* your data column is a date.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.label: The schema mistaken for the data
teaching_moves.text: you have a field list, and you believe you have a dataset. *Warning sign:* you can name every column and no value.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.label: The sample that is not a sample
teaching_moves.text: you were sent good rows. *Warning sign:* somebody else chose which rows you saw.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.label: The populated field
teaching_moves.text: the column is never null because a default is written into it. *Warning sign:* completeness with no variance.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.label: Consent assumed from access
teaching_moves.text: you can read it, so you conclude you may use it. *Warning sign:* your permission column contains a system name rather than a person's answer.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.label: The wrong informant
teaching_moves.text: you asked the sponsor, who invited you, rather than the person who maintains the thing. *Warning sign:* your provenance and your invitation come from the same role.
teaching_moves.day_title: S034 · Data You Were Promised and Data You Have

teaching_moves.text: What was the question, as chartered, and did the investigation answer it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What did the investigation cost — your time, other people's time, and anything you consumed?
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What is the cheaper investigation you can now see, having done this one?
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What in this finding will the sponsor dislike, and what will they do with it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What has the spike's code done since the charter closed? **Item 3 is not a trick.** Almost every completed investigation reveals a cheaper one, and naming it is how a practice gets less expensive rather than more thorough.
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The recommendation in the conclusion
teaching_moves.text: the finding tells the reader what to do, and the evidence becomes decorative. *Warning sign:* your conclusions section is shorter than your next-steps section.
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The rescued bound
teaching_moves.text: the limit was extended, quietly, because the answer was nearly there. *Warning sign:* your method describes more work than your charter authorised and does not say so.
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The absent cost
teaching_moves.text: the finding reports what was learned and not what it took. *Warning sign:* your document would read identically if the investigation had taken four times as long.
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The confirmed set
teaching_moves.text: every question came back yes. *Warning sign:* you are pleased with the finding.
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The smoothed data
teaching_moves.text: [S034](/wiki/seminars/S034.md)'s blocking absence has become a line in a risk table. *Warning sign:* a thing that was blocking now has a mitigation.
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The quiet retention
teaching_moves.text: the code was kept and the finding does not mention it. *Warning sign:* there is no disposal line at all.
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The unreadable evidence
teaching_moves.text: the evidence section is a narrative in which observations and inferences are interleaved. *Warning sign:* a reader has to trust you in order to use it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S035 · A Feasibility Finding ⊘

teaching_moves.text: Sketch your idea in one minute, by hand, on one sheet. Keep it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.text: List five details you left out. For each, write the conversation it would have started.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.text: Which of those five conversations is about your idea, and which are about something else?
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.text: You show somebody a finished-looking artefact and they say it looks great. What did you learn?
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.text: Producing the refined version costs you nothing extra. Give the reason not to. **Item 5 is the session's problem and it does not have a settled answer.** The argument for stripping detail was built when detail had a price. It no longer does.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.label: The costless polish
teaching_moves.text: the refined version took no longer, so you showed it. *Warning sign:* you did not decide to polish it; you just did not decide not to.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.label: The irrelevant argument
teaching_moves.text: the room spends its time on the equipment type, the workforce assumption, or whether the thing fits the physical constraints of the job, and never reaches the idea. *Warning sign:* the best question of the session was about something you invented to fill a gap.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.label: The implied commitment
teaching_moves.text: a detail you added for plausibility is read as a decision. *Warning sign:* somebody asks who chose that, and you cannot remember choosing.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.label: The suppressed no
teaching_moves.text: it looks like real work, so the person softens. *Warning sign:* the feedback is entirely additive.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.label: The deck
teaching_moves.text: the artefact became a presentation, which is a thing people watch rather than change. *Warning sign:* it has a running order.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.label: The keepsake
teaching_moves.text: you cannot throw it away, so you defend it. *Warning sign:* the second version is the first version with amendments.
teaching_moves.day_title: S036 · Deliberate Low Fidelity

teaching_moves.text: Your prototype fails on the first real case. Write the sentence you say next.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.text: Write what the sponsor is thinking while you say it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.text: What did the failure remove from the plan? Be specific — a design option, a cost, a week, an assumption.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.text: You could fix it in an hour before the meeting. Give the reason not to.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.text: A failure that costs a fortnight and a failure that costs an afternoon are both failures. What is different about how you report them? **Item 2 is the session.** Most learners can produce a good sentence for item 1 and have never thought about who is receiving it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.label: The rescued prototype
teaching_moves.text: you fixed it first, so the demonstration succeeded and established nothing. *Warning sign:* nothing went wrong.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.label: The failure framed as a learning
teaching_moves.text: you said the word *learning* and moved on. *Warning sign:* your account contains no specific thing that changed.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.label: The private failure
teaching_moves.text: it broke, you fixed it, nobody was told. *Warning sign:* the only people who know are the people who built it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.label: The coached conclusion
teaching_moves.text: you talked the sponsor into a position rather than into a reading. *Warning sign:* they now believe the thing works.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.label: The expensive failure sold as cheap
teaching_moves.text: a fortnight of work broke and you reported it in the register of an afternoon's experiment. *Warning sign:* your account omits the price.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.label: The demonstration that could not fail
teaching_moves.text: the case was chosen, the data was prepared, the path was rehearsed. *Warning sign:* you knew the outcome before you began.
teaching_moves.day_title: S037 · The Prototype That Fails Immediately

teaching_moves.text: List everybody your idea touches. Mark each as user, buyer, budget holder, or blocker. Some are more than one.
teaching_moves.day_title: S038 · Testing with People Who Are Not the Buyer

teaching_moves.text: Which of them can tell you that this would not help them? Which of them cannot?
teaching_moves.day_title: S038 · Testing with People Who Are Not the Buyer

teaching_moves.text: Somebody says *this would be really useful*. What have you learned?
teaching_moves.day_title: S038 · Testing with People Who Are Not the Buyer

teaching_moves.text: You cannot get access to a real user. A model can produce a plausible one. What is your position, and what is the best argument against it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S038 · Testing with People Who Are Not the Buyer

teaching_moves.text: Who loses if this succeeds, and have they seen it? **Item 3 has a specific answer and most learners do not have it.** You have learned that they were polite. A compliment is the commonest class of bad conversational data and it is evidentially empty.
teaching_moves.day_title: S038 · Testing with People Who Are Not the Buyer

teaching_moves.label: The demonstration to the sponsor
teaching_moves.text: the only test was with the person who commissioned the work. *Warning sign:* your record has one population in it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S038 · Testing with People Who Are Not the Buyer

teaching_moves.label: The merged segment
teaching_moves.text: users, buyers and blockers are aggregated under a customer heading. *Warning sign:* your finding says *they* and means four different groups.
teaching_moves.day_title: S038 · Testing with People Who Are Not the Buyer

teaching_moves.text: Your plan will be read by somebody who does not want to read it. teaching_moves.text: What evidence would have made you choose the alternative?
teaching_moves.day_title: S056 · Can This Be Solved Without AI At All

teaching_moves.text: Who benefits from the AI answer, and were they in the room when the problem was described? **Item 4 is the session.** A rejection that no evidence could have reversed is not a rejection, and this programme has already said that once, in week one, about engagements. **Item 2 is where most people fail**, because they offer the status quo and call it an alternative.
teaching_moves.day_title: S056 · Can This Be Solved Without AI At All

teaching_moves.label: The straw alternative
teaching_moves.text: a non-AI option designed to lose. *Warning sign:* you enjoyed writing it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S056 · Can This Be Solved Without AI At All

teaching_moves.label: The status quo as alternative
teaching_moves.text: you offered *carry on as now* and treated it as a design. *Warning sign:* your alternative has no components.
teaching_moves.day_title: S056 · Can This Be Solved Without AI At All

teaching_moves.label: The unpriced comparison
teaching_moves.text: the alternative is costed and the AI option is described. *Warning sign:* one column has numbers and the other has adjectives.
teaching_moves.day_title: S056 · Can This Be Solved Without AI At All

teaching_moves.label: The retrofitted question
teaching_moves.text: asked after the model was chosen, to be answered rather than to decide anything. *Warning sign:* nothing you could have written would have changed the plan.
teaching_moves.day_title: S056 · Can This Be Solved Without AI At All

teaching_moves.label: The capability answer
teaching_moves.text: you justified the choice by what the technology can do rather than by what the problem requires. *Warning sign:* your justification would fit a different problem unchanged.
teaching_moves.day_title: S056 · Can This Be Solved Without AI At All

teaching_moves.label: The unowned interest
teaching_moves.text: nobody in the record has anything to gain. *Warning sign:* your organisation is selling the thing you chose and the record does not mention it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S056 · Can This Be Solved Without AI At All

teaching_moves.text: Under an effort test, how much of your last delivery was in scope?
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.text: You configured an agent, wrote no model code, and handed it over. Effort test: in scope?
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.text: Where exactly is the boundary in your engagement? Name what is on each side.
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.text: Your test excludes something that can cause the harm the regime exists to prevent. What is it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.text: Your test includes something harmless. What does that cost? **Item 2 is the whole argument.** Under an effort test, the fastest and most consequential work in modern delivery escapes governance entirely — you did no model work, so nothing applies, and the customer is now running something that acts. **Items 4 and 5 are the assessed work**, because a test whose author has found no fault in it has not been read by its author.
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.label: The effort test in disguise
teaching_moves.text: the wording changed and the question did not. *Warning sign:* your test's answer depends on how much work you did.
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.label: The unlocatable boundary
teaching_moves.text: you can describe it in an organisational chart and not in credentials. *Warning sign:* you cannot say who can change the artefact next month.
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.label: The excluded configuration
teaching_moves.text: an off-the-shelf agent, configured by you, placed in a consequential workflow, and out of scope because you authored nothing. *Warning sign:* your test's line is *did we write it*.
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.label: The faultless test
teaching_moves.text: you found nothing wrong with your own test. *Warning sign:* you wrote it and then looked for confirmation.
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.label: The everything test
teaching_moves.text: it catches all your deliverables. *Warning sign:* you feel safe, and nobody will comply.
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.label: The orphaned exclusion
teaching_moves.text: you named the excluded case and then did nothing, because the regime did not require it. *Warning sign:* your answer to the last element is that it is out of scope.
teaching_moves.day_title: S057 · The Scope Test That Survives Agentic Delivery

teaching_moves.text: Look at any assessment your organisation holds. When was it last true?
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.text: What in your process would cause somebody to reopen it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.text: Take one claim from an assessment. What measurement would show it false?
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.text: Your review fires. What does it cost, in whose time?
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.text: If nobody reopens it for a year, what breaks — and who finds out? **Item 1 usually cannot be answered from the document itself**, which is the finding. **Item 4 is the one people skip**, and it decides whether anything you build here will ever run.
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.label: The one-shot assessment
teaching_moves.text: written to clear a gate, never reopened, describing a system that stopped existing. *Warning sign:* it was completed in one sitting.
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.label: The calendar trigger
teaching_moves.text: refresh annually, with nobody owning the calendar. *Warning sign:* your trigger has a date in it and no actor.
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.label: The unversioned document
teaching_moves.text: it changed, and nothing records what. *Warning sign:* the revision history has one row.
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.label: The unfalsifiable claim
teaching_moves.text: a commitment nothing could disturb. *Warning sign:* you cannot say what observation would embarrass it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.label: The unpriced ritual
teaching_moves.text: you designed a review nobody can afford, so it will not run. *Warning sign:* your review requires a meeting.
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.label: The wrong home
teaching_moves.text: correctly filed, permanently unread. *Warning sign:* you had to look up where it goes.
teaching_moves.day_title: S058 · Impact Assessment as a Living Document

teaching_moves.text: Where in your system does an output affect what happens to a person?
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.text: Who decides whether that proceeds? Name them, not their role.
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.text: What are they looking at when they decide?
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.text: Your regime has no legitimate way to say *we cannot comply yet*. What happens?
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.text: Could you have described your system slightly differently and avoided the classification? Be honest. **Item 4 has an answer everybody in the room has seen.** People do not stop shipping. **They stop recording.** Item 5 is the one nobody volunteers, and the willingness to answer it is the disposition this session is for.
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.label: The category exercise
teaching_moves.text: you classified it and stopped. *Warning sign:* your artefact ends with a label.
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.label: The absent decider
teaching_moves.text: the decision exists and nobody made it. *Warning sign:* your record names a function.
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.label: The permanent deviation
teaching_moves.text: recorded, approved, never revisited. *Warning sign:* it has no expiry, and nobody minded.
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.label: The escalation as decision
teaching_moves.text: you passed it upwards and treated the passing as resolution. *Warning sign:* nothing changed and nobody said no.
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.label: The unrecorded refusal
teaching_moves.text: you declined, verbally, in a meeting. *Warning sign:* nobody outside the room could find out that it happened.
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.label: The scope dodge
teaching_moves.text: you narrowed the system's description until the classification did not apply. *Warning sign:* the description changed and the system did not.
teaching_moves.day_title: S059 · Sensitive Use, and the Decision It Forces

teaching_moves.text: What changed because of this assessment?
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.text: Who is doing something differently, and can they name what?
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.text: Which of your findings is a legitimate engineering trade-off rather than a violation?
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What did you deliberately not give the team yet, and when will you?
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.text: If this assessment were deleted tomorrow, what would be lost? **Item 2 is the assessment's centre of gravity.** Item 3 is the one candidates skip, and skipping it is expensive: **a legitimate engineering trade-off scored as a violation teaches a team to ignore the scorer**, and a scorer a team ignores has cost more than its findings were worth.
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The sign-off
teaching_moves.text: a complete, careful, approved assessment that changed nothing. *Warning sign:* your answer to opening item 2 names nobody.
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The dump
teaching_moves.text: every finding given to the team at once, in one meeting, as a list. *Warning sign:* you are pleased with the volume, and nothing has moved since.
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The pre-emptive backlog
teaching_moves.text: tracked items created before the team saw them. *Warning sign:* somebody found out they had a new task by being assigned one.
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The merged document
teaching_moves.text: the record and the action plan are one artefact. *Warning sign:* you have a status column in your permanent record.
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The violation that was a decision
teaching_moves.text: a deliberate engineering trade-off written up as non-compliance. *Warning sign:* the team's response was to explain, and you did not change the finding.
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The generic work item
teaching_moves.text: an acceptance criterion nobody can check and a reason that would fit anything. *Warning sign:* it could be pasted into another project unchanged.
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The complete assessment
teaching_moves.text: nothing is unassessed. *Warning sign:* your unassessed list is empty and your scope test has no hole.
teaching_moves.day_title: S060 · An Assessment That Generates Work, Not a Sign-Off ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What question does each panel on your dashboard answer, and who asks it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.text: What are you collecting that nobody aggregates and nobody alerts on?
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.text: Where does a correlation identifier get assigned in your system, and what happens to a request that arrives before that point?
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.text: Of logging, metrics and tracing, which would you drop first if the bill doubled — and on what basis?
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.text: If your entire observability configuration were deleted tonight, how long would it take to rebuild, and from what? **Item 2 is the one that hurts.** Most estates fail it immediately, and the failure is invisible because unaggregated telemetry costs money quietly and produces nothing loudly.
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.label: The inherited dashboard
teaching_moves.text: panels nobody chose, kept because removing them feels like losing something. *Warning sign:* you cannot name a person who looks at it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.label: Collect because you can
teaching_moves.text: telemetry retained because it was easy to emit. *Warning sign:* your answer on retention is "the default".
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.label: The click-built alert
teaching_moves.text: configuration made in a console, invisible to review, undiffable and unattributable. *Warning sign:* nobody can tell you who changed it or when.
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.label: The exception logged at every layer
teaching_moves.text: the same raised exception logged four times on its way up. *Warning sign:* your error volume is a function of your call depth.
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.label: The high-cardinality label
teaching_moves.text: a unique or near-unique string used as the value of a metric label. *Warning sign:* your metrics cost tracks your user count.
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.label: The late correlation identifier
teaching_moves.text: assigned after the first hop, so the first hop is invisible. *Warning sign:* your traces start at the second service and nobody has noticed.
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.label: Tracing as an incident tool
teaching_moves.text: expecting a trace to tell you why production broke. Its purpose is not reactive; it is an optimisation instrument. *Warning sign:* your incident procedure opens with "check the traces".
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.label: The specification nobody can rebuild from
teaching_moves.text: a beautiful document, and the running configuration does not match it. *Warning sign:* your answer to opening item 5 is a person's name.
teaching_moves.day_title: S061 · Observability That Answers a Question

teaching_moves.text: What would you accept as evidence that a mitigation is implemented?
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.text: Who currently decides that a security work item is closed, and what do they look at when they decide?
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.text: Name one real fix in your system that would leave no trace in your repository.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.text: Who wrote your acceptance criteria, and who wrote the mitigation they check?
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.text: What schedules the re-check, and what happens if nobody runs it? **Item 3 is the session's centre of gravity.** A learner who cannot name one has not yet understood what the mechanism does not see.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.label: The assertion
teaching_moves.text: closure happens because somebody competent said so. *Warning sign:* the closing evidence is a meeting.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.label: The perpetual work item
teaching_moves.text: a real fix that leaves no trace, so the item regenerates on every run, forever. *Warning sign:* the same item has reappeared several times and somebody has started skipping it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.label: The self-marking criterion
teaching_moves.text: the acceptance criterion and the mitigation share an author, so they agree about whatever they both misunderstand. *Warning sign:* the criterion restates the mitigation in the imperative.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.label: The unscheduled derivation
teaching_moves.text: a well-designed procedure nobody runs. *Warning sign:* the last run's date is also the only run's date.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.label: The keyword hit
teaching_moves.text: a search matched text rather than behaviour. *Warning sign:* your evidence is a line in a file nothing imports.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.label: Naming as evidence
teaching_moves.text: a technology named in a document counted as deployed. *Warning sign:* your citation is to a design document. **This is [S054](/wiki/seminars/S054.md) arriving in production**, and it is the failure the file-and-location rule exists to prevent.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.label: The register that lists only the convenient gaps
teaching_moves.text: every entry is something outside your control. *Warning sign:* nothing in the register is your responsibility.
teaching_moves.day_title: S062 · Evidence-Derived Closure

teaching_moves.text: What is the minimum service quality your customer would actually accept — not what you intend to deliver?
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.text: Which of your alerts fired most recently, who received it, and what did they do?
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.text: Name a signal your system produces that no downstream process consumes.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.text: What would tell you an incident had happened if nobody reported it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.text: Who is woken up by your alerts, and have you asked them? **Item 1 is the session's instrument and almost everybody answers it wrong the first time**, because the honest answer is lower than the answer a delivery team wants to give.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.label: Alert fatigue
teaching_moves.text: everything pages, so nothing does. *Warning sign:* somebody has a mail rule, and it is not a secret.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.label: The aspirational service level
teaching_moves.text: the objective is what the team hopes to deliver, set by the team, never put to the customer. *Warning sign:* your service level was agreed in a room the customer was not in.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.label: The orphan analyser
teaching_moves.text: a scanner or report produces genuine findings that no process consumes. *Warning sign:* the reports are good, and no work item anywhere references one.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.label: The blameful account
teaching_moves.text: the remedy for an incident is that somebody should be more careful. *Warning sign:* your corrective action is training.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.label: The unreported incident
teaching_moves.text: nothing was reported, so nothing happened. *Warning sign:* your incident count is a function of customer patience rather than of system behaviour.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.label: The target of total availability
teaching_moves.text: no error budget, so every change is a breach and the objective is quietly ignored. *Warning sign:* nobody has ever cited the objective in a decision.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.label: The undeleted alert
teaching_moves.text: you agreed it expects no action and you kept it anyway. *Warning sign:* your deletion record is empty and your alert count went up.
teaching_moves.day_title: S063 · The Incident You Did Not See

teaching_moves.text: What does one unit of your system's work cost, and what is the unit?
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.text: Which design decision in your system is the most expensive to run, and was it chosen for that reason?
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.text: What does your observability cost, and against which signals?
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.text: What happens to the bill if usage grows and nothing else changes?
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.text: Who will hold this model after you leave, and can they run it? **Item 1 is the one that separates a cost model from a bill.** A figure per compute hour is a bill. A figure per unit of the customer's work is a model.
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.label: The gross benefit
teaching_moves.text: a return offered with no cost beside it. *Warning sign:* your value document has one column and it is the good one.
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.label: The infrastructure unit
teaching_moves.text: cost per node, per hour, per instance, per token. *Warning sign:* the customer cannot tell what one of their own transactions costs.
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.label: The forecast that never met telemetry
teaching_moves.text: a model built once from estimates, never refined against what actually happened. *Warning sign:* every input is an estimate and none is dated.
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.label: Free observability
teaching_moves.text: telemetry treated as overhead rather than as spend, so nothing in the model ever argues against collecting more. *Warning sign:* it is not a line.
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.label: The optimisation nobody measured
teaching_moves.text: a change adopted because a tool labelled it an efficiency, with no measurement of the thing it optimised. *Warning sign:* your justification is the name of a feature. **The openly published playbook demonstrates this failure against itself**, in a checklist recommending a set of efficiency measures that its own sibling page argues may each be net negative.
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.label: The model you take with you
teaching_moves.text: the capability leaves when the team does. *Warning sign:* the model is a spreadsheet on your machine, and the handover plan says "we will share it".
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.label: The dominated term nobody found
teaching_moves.text: the model is accurate today and wrong at scale, because nothing states which term grows fastest. *Warning sign:* item 4 was answered with "it scales".
teaching_moves.day_title: S064 · Cost as a Design Constraint

teaching_moves.text: Which claim about your running system rests on somebody's word rather than on evidence?
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What is on your invisible-fix register, and what is the most serious thing on it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.text: Under what conditions should this system not be operated?
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What did you stop collecting, and what did you stop alerting on?
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.text: If you disappeared this evening, what would the operator not be able to find out? **Item 3 is the one candidates skip.** A readiness argument with no conditions attached is a statement that the system is always ready, which nobody believes and nobody wrote down.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The demonstration
teaching_moves.text: readiness argued from a working system in front of you. *Warning sign:* your argument requires you to be present.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The unconditioned readiness
teaching_moves.text: no circumstance is named under which the system should not run. *Warning sign:* item 3 is blank or generic.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The convenient register
teaching_moves.text: every invisible fix is somebody else's platform, somebody else's tenant, somebody else's contract. *Warning sign:* nothing in it is your responsibility.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The console configuration
teaching_moves.text: the observability is excellent and lives where nobody can review it. *Warning sign:* your evidence is a screenshot.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The intentional trigger
teaching_moves.text: the re-derivation is scheduled "each sprint" with no actor and no state change. *Warning sign:* the owner is the team.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The aspirational floor
teaching_moves.text: the service level is what you hope to deliver, and the explicit sentence is missing. *Warning sign:* the customer has not seen it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The model that only you can run
teaching_moves.text: nobody on the customer's side has opened it. *Warning sign:* your date field is a plan.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The complete argument
teaching_moves.text: nothing is outside it. *Warning sign:* your exclusions list is empty and you are pleased about it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S065 · An Operational Readiness Argument ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What was the value of your headline measure the week before you arrived, and how do you know?
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.text: Who measured it, with what instrument, and does that instrument still exist?
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.text: What result would make the customer conclude this had not worked?
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.text: What else changed in the same period?
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.text: If you cannot establish the baseline, what will you say instead? **Item 3 is missing from the corpus's entire discovery apparatus.** Its question bank asks in every block what good would look like and how improvement would be measured. It asks nowhere what result would mean it had failed. That absence is the reason this item is here.
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.label: The retrospective baseline
teaching_moves.text: the before state estimated after the fact by the people who built the after state. *Warning sign:* your before figure and your after figure were produced in the same meeting.
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.label: The instrument you do not own
teaching_moves.text: the measurement depends on a system the customer does not run or will not share. *Warning sign:* your measurement plan begins with "we would need access to".
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.label: The unfalsifiable improvement
teaching_moves.text: no result would have counted against it. *Warning sign:* item 3 is blank, and you did not notice it was blank.
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.label: The moved measure
teaching_moves.text: the definition changed between before and after, usually improving. *Warning sign:* the after measure is better instrumented than the before one.
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.label: The baseline that is a target
teaching_moves.text: the before value is what somebody said it should have been. *Warning sign:* the figure is round.
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.label: The measure nobody had
teaching_moves.text: you are the first person ever to measure this, and you are presenting it as an improvement. *Warning sign:* your before column is empty and your after column is full, and the document reads as a success.
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.label: The reconstructed memory
teaching_moves.text: the baseline comes from an interview conducted after the result. *Warning sign:* your source for the before state is a person rather than a record.
teaching_moves.day_title: S066 · The Baseline Nobody Measured

teaching_moves.text: Who, by name, is responsible for establishing that your system caused the change?
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.text: What else could have caused it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.text: A previous solution already exists. How do you separate its effect from yours, and both from the learning that happened alongside them?
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.text: Which of your metric definitions contains the word *attributable*, and what work is that word doing?
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.text: What would you accept as evidence that your system did **not** cause the change? **Item 1 is the session.** Most answers are a role nobody holds, a team, or a silence.
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.label: The circular metric
teaching_moves.text: a measure defined as the change caused by the system, then offered as evidence the system caused a change. *Warning sign:* the word *attributable* appears in the definition and nobody has noticed it is doing the work.
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.label: The unassigned responsibility
teaching_moves.text: everybody agrees causation matters and nobody owns it. *Warning sign:* your governance record has an owner for every risk and none for the attribution.
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.label: The co-timed change
teaching_moves.text: a reorganisation, a policy change, a price change, a seasonal shift. *Warning sign:* you cannot say what else happened in the period.
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.label: The learning confound claimed as yours
teaching_moves.text: the customer improved at the task while using the system, and the whole change is claimed. *Warning sign:* you delivered training inside the measurement window and it is not in the list.
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.label: The engineered denominator
teaching_moves.text: the cost side is instrumented and the return side is elicited, and the ratio is presented as though both were measured. *Warning sign:* one side of your ratio comes from telemetry and the other from a menu.
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.label: The role that nobody holds
teaching_moves.text: attribution assigned to "the programme" or "the steering group". *Warning sign:* you cannot email the owner.
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.label: The unexaminable separation
teaching_moves.text: a method for separating causes is asserted and not described. *Warning sign:* your document says "controlled for".
teaching_moves.day_title: S067 · Attribution, and Who Is Responsible for It

teaching_moves.text: Where did every input to your model come from, and who supplied it?
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.text: Which claim in the framework could your output contradict?
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.text: If the output is wrong, who is wrong?
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.text: What in the model was measured, and what was elicited?
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.text: Your model runs a simulation over a distribution. Where did the distribution come from? **Item 2 is the instrument.** It has no answer, and finding that out is the session.
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.label: The borrowed authority
teaching_moves.text: the figure circulates with the framework's name attached and rests entirely on what somebody said in a workshop. *Warning sign:* the output is being forwarded and the input sheet is not.
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.label: The unfalsifiable output
teaching_moves.text: no proposition anywhere in the framework could contradict it. *Warning sign:* you cannot say what would make the model wrong, and you had not tried.
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.label: The example bank as benchmark
teaching_moves.text: illustrative thresholds treated as normal ranges. *Warning sign:* you described a real customer's figure as high or low, and cannot say against what.
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.label: The precise simulation over an invented distribution
teaching_moves.text: spurious precision. *Warning sign:* your output is stated more finely than any input's provenance would support.
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.label: The asymmetric ratio
teaching_moves.text: an instrumented denominator and an elicited numerator, presented as one measurement. *Warning sign:* one side of the ratio has telemetry and the other has a menu.
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.label: Specimen answers become norms
teaching_moves.text: figures embedded in illustrative response menus internalised as the plausible range. *Warning sign:* you hold an expectation about what a customer's number should be and cannot say where it came from. **These are the items to quarantine most aggressively.**
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.label: Provenance in an appendix
teaching_moves.text: the classification exists and nobody who reads the output sees it. *Warning sign:* the summary page has numbers and no marks.
teaching_moves.day_title: S068 · A Number-Generating Apparatus With No Numbers

teaching_moves.text: What is the result, in one sentence, with no qualifying clause?
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.text: Who is worse off if you report it, and are you one of them?
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.text: What is the strongest honest reading in your favour, and is it honest?
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.text: Where in your organisation's prepared answers does this result already have a rebuttal waiting?
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.text: Where will this be recorded, and who will be able to find it in a year? **Item 4 is the one nobody expects.** Most organisations have prepared an answer to your result before you obtained it, and you can usually find it in the material you were given during onboarding.
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.label: The buried contradiction
teaching_moves.text: the finding that contradicts the headline claim is recorded somewhere nobody reads. *Warning sign:* the most interesting thing you learned this engagement is in a slide's notes field. **This is not hypothetical:** in the corpus behind this programme, a finding that a coding assistant could not be asked to add a feature end to end on a mature production codebase — because the generated code reused outdated patterns and ignored architectural constraints — **directly contradicts the collection's own headline velocity claims and is buried in speaker notes.**
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.label: The readiness deflection
teaching_moves.text: the shortfall is reattributed to the customer's constraints. *Warning sign:* your explanation was written before your result existed.
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.label: The qualifying clause
teaching_moves.text: the result is true and the sentence containing it is not. *Warning sign:* your one-sentence result has three commas.
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.label: The synthetic failure
teaching_moves.text: a composed failure narrative offered in place of a real one. *Warning sign:* your failure case is illustrative and your successes are specific. **The corpus does exactly this**: every case study succeeds, and its single failure narrative is a synthetic composite, fictional by its own admission.
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.label: The delayed report
teaching_moves.text: the result waits for a better one. *Warning sign:* you are re-running the measurement before you have reported the first.
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.label: The unrecorded refusal
teaching_moves.text: you declined something, correctly, and nowhere says so. *Warning sign:* the only refusal in your engagement's record is in somebody's memory.
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.label: The bad-news sandwich
teaching_moves.text: the result is between two good ones. *Warning sign:* your document has a structure your result did not require.
teaching_moves.day_title: S069 · Reporting a Result That Undermines You

teaching_moves.text: State your claim in one sentence, and say what class of claim it is: causal, associative or descriptive.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.text: Which part of it rests on something nobody measured?
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.text: Who is responsible for the attribution, and have they accepted?
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.text: What result would have meant this did not work, and did that get written down before you looked?
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.text: Which of your figures would you remove if you had to defend the claim to somebody hostile? **Item 1 is where most candidates fail before they start**, by writing a causal sentence and classifying it as descriptive, or the reverse.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The misclassified sentence
teaching_moves.text: a causal claim wearing descriptive language, or a descriptive one dressed as causal. *Warning sign:* your sentence contains a verb like *drove* and your classification says observation.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The reconstructed baseline
teaching_moves.text: a before state assembled after the result by people who wanted the result. *Warning sign:* both figures were produced in the same week.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The retrofitted disconfirmation
teaching_moves.text: the failure condition written once the result was known, and it conveniently did not occur. *Warning sign:* it has no date, or its date is the date of the report.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The unowned attribution
teaching_moves.text: nobody was asked, so nobody refused. *Warning sign:* you have no refusal and no acceptance.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The undowngraded claim
teaching_moves.text: separation was not achieved and the sentence still says the system caused it. *Warning sign:* your competing-explanation list is longer than your analysis.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The appendix provenance
teaching_moves.text: the classifications exist and nobody reading the number sees them. *Warning sign:* the page that will be forwarded has figures and no marks.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.label: The absent bad news
teaching_moves.text: no unfavourable result and no account of looking for one. *Warning sign:* everything you measured supported your position.
teaching_moves.day_title: S070 · A Measurement You Will Defend ⊘

teaching_moves.text: Name the thing you are handing over. Not the system — the list of objects. How long is your list?
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.text: Which item on your list is currently held in a place that is not the repository?
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.text: Which item, if you are honest, has no plausible receiver at this customer?
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.text: What happens to that item when you leave?
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.text: If somebody accepted your handover, what would they have done? Describe the act. **Item 5 is where the exercise usually collapses.** Most learners can name a handover and cannot name an acceptance, which means what they have designed is a departure with paperwork.
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.label: Access mistaken for transfer
teaching_moves.text: permissions are granted, the manifest is marked complete, and nothing has moved. *Warning sign:* your acceptance condition is a thing you do rather than a thing they do.
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.label: The everything manifest
teaching_moves.text: every artefact of the engagement is listed at equal weight, so no receiver can tell what matters. *Warning sign:* your manifest has no order, or its order is the order you built things in.
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.label: The orphan you did not look for
teaching_moves.text: the evaluation harness and the cost model have no owner because they belong to nobody's job description on either side. *Warning sign:* every line has an owner and you found that easy.
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.label: The invisible location
teaching_moves.text: an object lives in a spreadsheet, a personal drive, a chat history or somebody's memory, and appears on the manifest as though it lived with the code. *Warning sign:* you cannot say the path.
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.label: The willing under-authorised owner
teaching_moves.text: the person who most wants the system is named against every line, and holds no budget, no access and no mandate. *Warning sign:* a single name appears against most of the difficult lines.
teaching_moves.day_title: S071 · What Actually Transfers

teaching_moves.text: Take the last real failure this system had. Write down how you knew it had started.
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.text: Would your answer to item 1 be available to somebody who is not you? Say how they would get it.
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.text: At the first branch in your diagnosis, what evidence distinguishes the two paths?
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.text: What is the point at which the operator should stop and escalate, and to whom — by role, not by name?
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.text: What in your runbook is true only because of something you happen to remember? **Item 5 has no honest answer from the inside.** That is the point of the session: you cannot audit your own context, so somebody else has to execute the document while you watch.
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.label: The runbook that assumes its author
teaching_moves.text: every step is correct and several are unperformable by anybody else. *Warning sign:* a step begins with "check that the pipeline looks normal".
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.label: The happy-path runbook
teaching_moves.text: it documents the procedure and not the failure, so it is a description of the system rather than a response to it. *Warning sign:* it contains no branch.
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.label: The escalation to a person
teaching_moves.text: the route ends at a name, a personal phone number or a private channel. *Warning sign:* the name is yours.
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.label: The unstartable runbook
teaching_moves.text: its trigger is a feeling. Something seems slow; the drafts look worse than usual. *Warning sign:* your entry condition contains a comparative with no reference value.
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.label: The rescue
teaching_moves.text: the executor stalls, you explain, everybody feels the session went well, and no defect was recorded. *Warning sign:* you spoke.
teaching_moves.day_title: S072 · Runbooks, and the Operator Who Is Not You

teaching_moves.text: Where did the evaluation set come from? Name the selection rule, not the source.
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.text: Who chose each threshold, on what basis, and is that basis recorded anywhere but in your memory?
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.text: Suppose the harness runs after you leave and the result is bad. Name the person who is obliged to do something, and name what they are obliged to do.
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.text: What would make this harness stop being a test of the live system without anybody noticing?
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.text: Is the cost model in the same class of object as the harness? Say why or why not. **Item 3 is the session.** A harness whose failing result obliges nobody is a decoration, and you can transfer a decoration perfectly.
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.label: The frozen set
teaching_moves.text: the evaluation data was assembled once, the live distribution moved, and the harness now passes reliably while measuring something that no longer occurs. *Warning sign:* nobody can say when the set last changed.
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.label: The threshold with no parent
teaching_moves.text: values transferred as numbers, with the reasoning left in the head of the person who set them on a busy afternoon. *Warning sign:* you can state the value instantly and the reason slowly.
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.label: The consequence-free result
teaching_moves.text: the harness runs, the result is recorded, and nothing in the organisation is arranged to respond to it. *Warning sign:* your answer to "who acts?" is a team rather than a role.
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.label: The harness that requires you
teaching_moves.text: running it involves a step only you can perform, an environment only you can reach, or a judgement only you can make. *Warning sign:* the run procedure contains the word "then check".
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.label: The orphaned instrument
teaching_moves.text: the harness and the cost model are handed to the most technically capable receiver rather than to the one whose work depends on their output. *Warning sign:* the named owner has never asked to see a result.
teaching_moves.day_title: S073 · The Evaluation Harness They Inherit

teaching_moves.text: In your engagement, what event would currently cause the environments to be removed? Name the event, not the intention.
teaching_moves.day_title: S074 · Estate Hygiene, Triggered by a Register

teaching_moves.text: Who would have to remember? What are they doing that week?
teaching_moves.day_title: S074 · Estate Hygiene, Triggered by a Register

teaching_moves.text: An environment survives its project and gets used for the next customer. Name the harm. Be specific about what crosses.
teaching_moves.day_title: S074 · Estate Hygiene, Triggered by a Register

teaching_moves.text: Somebody leaves your team on a Friday. List every act that ought to follow, and say who performs each.
teaching_moves.day_title: S074 · Estate Hygiene, Triggered by a Register

teaching_moves.text: When each of those acts has been performed, what artefact exists that says so? **Item 5 has no answer in the source, and that is not an oversight you should be comfortable with.** The trigger is mechanised to the level of a state machine and there is no evidentiary requirement that the teardown was performed at all.
teaching_moves.day_title: S074 · Estate Hygiene, Triggered by a Register

teaching_moves.label: The trigger that is an intention
